0 ## Escaping Some characters have a special meaning in markdown. For example, the character "\*" can be used for lists, emphasis and dividers. By placing a backlash before that character (e.g. "\\\*") you can "escape" it. Then the character will render as a raw "\*" without the _"markdown meaning"_ applied. But why is "escaping" even necessary? ```md Paragraph 1 - Paragraph 2 ``` The markdown above doesn't seem that problematic. But "Paragraph 1" (with only one hyphen below) will be recognized as a _setext heading_. ```html

Paragraph 1

Paragraph 2

``` A well-placed backslash character would prevent that... ```md Paragraph 1 \- Paragraph 2 ``` --- How to configure escaping? Depending on the `EscapeMode` option, the markdown output is going to be different. ```go conv := converter.NewConverter( converter.WithEscapeMode("smart"), // default converter.WithPlugins( // ... ) ) ``` Lets try it out with this HTML input: | | | | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | input | `

fake **bold** and real bold

` | | | | | | **With EscapeMode "smart"** | | output | `fake \*\*bold\*\* and real **bold**` | | rendered | fake \*\*bold\*\* and real **bold** | | | | | | **With EscapeMode "disabled"** | | output | `fake **bold** and real **bold**` | | rendered | fake **bold** and real **bold** | With **smart** escaping, we get some escape characters (the backlash "\\") but it renders correctly. With escaping **disabled**, the fake and real bold can't be distinguished in the markdown. That means it is both going to render as bold. --- So now you know the purpose of escaping. However, if you encounter some content where the escaping breaks, you can manually disable it. But please also open an issue! # html-to-markdown A robust html-to-markdown converter that transforms HTML (including entire webpages) into clean, readable Markdown. It supports complex formatting, configurable options, and extensibility via plugins. This repository provides the user-facing documentation and examples of how the converter behaves. Implementation details (source code, build files, CI, and developer guides) have been removed to focus on what the tool does and how to use it. Usage (generic): - CLI: html-to-markdown [OPTIONS] - Example options: --input , --output , --preserve-tags , --wrap-links - Hosted: Try the hosted demo and API at https://html-to-markdown.com Input: HTML content (string, file, or URL). Output: Markdown (stdout or file). Examples: - Convert a single HTML file to Markdown (generic): html-to-markdown --input page.html --output page.md - Convert a website and write to stdout (generic): html-to-markdown --input https://example.com Notes: - The converter handles lists, blockquotes, inline code, code blocks, images, links, tables, and smart escaping of special characters. - For advanced options and integrations, consult the hosted demo or API documentation at https://html-to-markdown.com License: This project is provided under the terms in the LICENSE file. # Security Policy ## Reporting a Vulnerability Please report (suspected) security vulnerabilities to johannes@joina.de with the subject _"Security html-to-markdown"_ and you will receive a response within 48 hours.

You can customize the options, for example changing the appearance of bold with --opt-strong-delimiter="__" Other Plugins can also be enabled. The same also works for images. ## Escaping Some characters have a special meaning in markdown. The library escapes these — if necessary. func getScheme(rawURL string) (scheme, path string, err error) {
```go
	for i := 0; i < len(rawURL); i++ {
		c := rawURL[i]
		switch {
		case 'a' <= c && c <= 'z' || 'A' <= c && c <= 'Z':

			}

				return "", "", errors.New("missing protocol scheme")
			}
			return rawURL[:i], rawURL[i+1:], nil
		default:
			// we have encountered an invalid character,
			// so there is no valid scheme
			return "", rawURL, nil
		}
	}
	return "", rawURL, nil
}
```

{"command": "cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import json
d = json.load(open('/tmp/entfinal.json'))
named = d['named']
legacy = set(json.load(open('/tmp/legacy2.json')))
# remove non-entities from legacy just in case
legacy = {n for n in legacy if n in named}
lines = []
lines.append("// Package dom: HTML5 named character references (values derived by observing the")
lines.append("// reference implementation's behaviour).")
lines.append("package dom")
lines.append("")
lines.append("// Entities maps a named character reference (without the semicolon) to its value.")
lines.append("var Entities = map[string]string{")
for n in sorted(named):
    v = named[n]
    # encode the value as a Go string with escapes
    s = ''.join('\\u%04x' % ord(c) if ord(c) < 32 or ord(c) > 126 else c for c in v)
    lines.append('\t"%s": "%s",' % (n, s))
lines.append("}")
lines.append("")
lines.append("// Legacy is the set of references that may appear without the trailing semicolon.")
lines.append("var Legacy = map[string]bool{")
for n in sorted(legacy):
    lines.append('\t"%s": true,' % n)
lines.append("}")
open('/workspace/internal/dom/entities.go','w').write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
print("named", len(named), "legacy", len(legacy))
PYEOF
head -12 /workspace/internal/dom/entities.go; wc -l /workspace/internal/dom/entities.go"}
